title: Idempotent, adaptive sanity guard for private EKS control plane provisioning
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a Terraform module and orchestration harness that ensures idempotent, operatorless provisioning and upgrade of the Redwood Private EKS control plane. The module should provide adaptive sanity checks (preflight assertions, live health probes, and post-change verification) and a lightweight rollback decision API for automation consumers. The goal is to reduce failed upgrade windows, eliminate flaky partial-provision states, and provide clear human-readable remediation steps when assertions fail. This ticket covers module design, test harness, canary gating config, and integration points with the control-plane bootstrapper and our CI/CD pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module applies idempotently against an empty and an existing cluster without producing transient errors (repeatable applies produce no changes).
Preflight assertions catch missing KMS policy, mismatched VPC subnets, and incompatible control plane AMI/launch template before any irreversible changes are made.
Health probes (control-plane API reachability, etcd quorum, kube-apiserver certificate validity) run automatically during upgrades and surface structured results in CI logs.
A canary rollout path allows the module to apply to a single control-plane replica / test cluster and block fleet-wide promotion on assertion or probe failures.
Rollback hints and a one-click remediation guide are appended to the Terraform output and posted to the provision run URL when checks fail.
Automated integration tests exercising blue/green and patch upgrades are present in the terraform-module repo pipeline and pass in the dedicated QA account.

notes: Key design choices: (1) avoid kube-operators for control plane lifecycle; use Terraform driven orchestration + lightweight probe runner to reduce blast radius, (2) maintain explicit KMS+IAM preflight to prevent silent failures during kms-key rotation, (3) leverage module fingerprints to detect out-of-band drift and require manual reconciliation when detected.
